doc.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021

title: Audiences clapping on one and three
summary: Audience clapping on the wrong beats as a sign the music connects; music as communication.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: So have you ever been playing one of your solo numbers and the audience gets into it and they start clapping on one and three?
The worst. No. Yes it definitely has happened. Yeah. And there are some places maybe that do that more than others.
Yes that’s very interesting. Someone, it’s like you could do a sociological study about where that demarcation is.

Totally. Yeah. And I mean I just love that they’re, the fact that an audience is clapping to the music means that it’s connecting in some way. And like you were saying, for me, so much of music is connecting with others. It’s not just for myself. There is a lot about, for myself, of course. But so much is about sharing this. It’s a communication. It’s a language. I am thinking about the audience. I want to say something and I want them to be there with me.
